The cited mathematical scattering, impulse, and control-volume suppliers support the main conditional deductions; no prerequisite gap requires owner escalation if the local clarifications below are made.

findings.reason: Approved CM15 E10 and thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density support adding pushforward measures from disjoint incident-parameter intervals even when their angular images overlap. Clause (ii) currently defines a model sum only for disjoint image intervals, leaving valid overlap contributions undefined. Define the total density as the sum on overlaps and distinguish it from each branch contribution.

Clause (v) identifies relative angles with those of a centre-of-mass frame without defining that special frame. post-cm01-frames defines inertial frames as adapted charts and pthm-cm05-relative-reduction supplies the affine centre-of-mass curve; state the Galilean boost/chart in which that curve is at rest, or use relative-coordinate language alone.

Clause 2 and Fact [L2] claim exact free motion for rho(t1) >= R, while thm-cm-scattering-turning-point-and-global-branches proves the free-tail claim only for rho > R. Preserve the boundary case with a local uniqueness argument using U = 0 on [R,infinity) and U'(R) = 0, or match the supplier's strict inequality.

Clause (iii) states m' and (mv)' but gives only maps m and v. State that m and v are differentiable on I, as required by thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance, so the adopted identities have explicit regularity.

Clause 2 reintroduces a smooth-force motion and concludes J = 0, but J was introduced for the impulse-model motion in clause 1. State explicitly that the same candidate motion is being checked in the smooth branch, or state that the smooth motion's momentum jump vanishes and identify it with J under the joint hypothesis.

The consumed def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus defines its advector as u:O->R3, while continuum-motion supplies u:I×O->R3 and this theorem uses D_tu. Locally state D_tu = partial_t u + (D_x u)u, componentwise, as computed in thm-cm-local-momentum-balance. Also make the differentiability of the lumped m,v in clause 3 and the physical types and units of rho,u,sigma,b explicit.

The fixed-wall normal-reflection rule is an example-specific law, not a formal e = 1 member of post-cm15-impulse clause (ii), which is limited to finite-mass collinear two-label restitution. Keep the rule and calculation, but describe it as separately adopted and call e = 1 only an analogy or limit.

The refracting-shell interface rule is separately adopted, not supplied by post-cm15-impulse's collinear law; clarify this. The remark's 'glory concentration' is unsupported for the stated jump to zero, and theta = 0 is outside the defined branch domain. Classical glory treatments describe a smooth zero-angle deflection; remove the label or define a separate forward contribution ([Mott and Massey, “Semiclassical description of scattering”](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(59)90026-0)). Also identify b = 0 as an endpoint extension, not a branch value.

The remark says the hard-sphere and refracting-shell rules are adopted from post-cm15-impulse, although neither full rule is covered by its restricted clauses. Describe them as example-specific assumptions. After the cross-section repair, distinguish branch contributions from the summed model density on overlapping angular images.

The declared interval I = (0, 5/2) excludes t = 0, but the example imposes v(0) = 0 and uses the formula on 0 <= t < 2. Choose an open interval containing 0 or state the initial datum as a one-sided continuous extension.

The material-ball check should specify its control motion, for example psi(t,X) = exp(alpha t)X, and declare units for alpha, rho0, and p0. The elbow calculation gives the net external resultant required by the steady momentum balance; it does not isolate a pressure-free 'momentum-flux part.' Equal port pressures and inviscid walls do not determine the wall pressure traction. Recast 3.578 N as the conditional net resultant or provide boundary-stress data for a force decomposition. The cited [Moore §11.7](https://eng.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Mechanical_Engineering/Mechanics_Map_%28Moore_2nd_Edition%29/11%3A_Impulse_and_Momentum_in_Particles/11.07%3A_Steady-Flow_Devices) supplies the net steady-flow force relation.
